resources.string: First launch: the bundled Linux environment and game files will be unpacked (about 2 GB, needs ~4 GB of free space).
Open the log to see details.
VirGL – Mesa virpipe → virglrenderer → Mali GLES
Hardware mode goes through virglrenderer to the Mali GPU; software mode uses llvmpipe when something goes wrong.
Virtual gamepad: D-pad, mouse buttons, wheel and a few hotkeys. Finger drags outside the buttons keep working as the touchpad. The ≡ button collapses the pad.
Compatibility mode for proot (slower, use if the game does not start)
Applied. Restart the app to take effect.
The unpacked Linux environment and all local saves will be deleted. The next launch will unpack everything again.
Factorio is running in the background

Version %1$s
Package: %2$s
Renderer: %3$s

Runs the official aarch64 Linux build of Factorio inside a bundled Arch Linux ARM root filesystem via proot (no root required) and displays it with the embedded Lorie X11 server.

Factorio is a trademark of Wube Software. You need your own legally obtained copy of the game files.
The game is not installed. Pick a tar archive of your own Factorio build (.tar, .tar.gz, .tar.xz, .tar.zst).
The game is installed. Delete the archive you just used? It is usually 1.5 GB and no longer needed.
The storage provider did not let the app delete %s. Remove it with a file manager.
Unpacks another Factorio archive over the current installation. Saves and settings inside the game folder are replaced too, so copy them out first if you need them.
Copies a save file into the game’s saves folder. Factorio saves are ordinary .zip files.
Copies a mod .zip into the game’s mods folder. Enable it in the game’s Mods menu afterwards.
CPU uses the llvmpipe software renderer: slow but works everywhere. VirGL sends the game’s OpenGL to the phone GPU through virglrenderer, which is what makes it playable.
The X screen the game renders into. Lower resolution = fewer pixels = higher FPS, but a blurrier picture.
Extra command line arguments for the Factorio binary. --video-memory-usage=low and --max-texture-size keep the atlas memory small, which matters on a phone.
Shows the virtual gamepad over the game. Finger drags outside the buttons still work as a touchpad, so you can walk with the left thumb and aim with the right one.
Opens the layout editor: drag buttons around, add new ones, change what they do. The result is stored as JSON and can be exported later.
Throws away your layout and restores the bundled one for the current mode (touch or gamepad).

Replaces the D-pad with an analogue stick and lays the buttons out like a controller. The game still sees keyboard and mouse: Android does not let apps create a real joystick device, so Factorio’s own "gamepad" input mode cannot be used. A real controller paired with the phone is forwarded automatically.
Language of this launcher only. The game has its own language setting.
Starts a small PulseAudio server next to the game and routes it to Android audio.
Workaround for devices where proot’s seccomp acceleration misbehaves (game crashes immediately). Slower, but more compatible.
Drag a button to move it, tap to select. Changes are saved when you press Save or go back.
